summary: Rebuilds no longer leak kernel memory. Replicad 1.1's fuse, cut and intersect leave their native builder to garbage collection and never delete the raw result handle, which keeps each result's topology alive for the life of the kernel module; its translate, rotate, mirror and scale also leak their builder and raw handle and consume their input; and its Plane builds coordinate transforms the kernel never reads, leaking a gp_Trsf and two gp_Ax3 for every sketch placement. The kernel now runs these operations through owned adapters in cadKernelBuilders.ts: fuse, cut and common; translate, rotate, mirror and scale, which leave their input intact; and all-edge fillet and chamfer. Each repeats Replicad's native calls exactly, including the second Build() and SimplifyResult(true, true, 0.001) after a boolean's constructor, which is part of today's geometry, borrows its inputs, returns a new shape and deletes its builder, raw result and every temporary in finally, also when the native operation throws. Sketch placement uses CadKernelPlane, which owns only the origin, x direction and normal that Replicad's Plane gives; the sketch axis, faces with holes, the extrusion vector and the revolve axis are built and deleted by the kernel. Extrude, Revolve, booleans, Join, Cut, linear and circular patterns, Mirror, Transform, loft, segment sweep, Pocket and inch STL import use the adapters; Shell and selected-edge fillet and chamfer already owned their builders. Over 100 rebuilds of each part in one module, with the event loop turning between rebuilds as in the worker, OpenCascade memory grew by 27.1 to 244.1 MiB on 5 of 12 parts at 0.0.789 and by none at 0.0.793; rebuilt back to back it grew by up to 979.1 MiB, and an imported STL body cut by a slot grew from 1,543.1 to 4,023.1 MiB, where 5 of 100 rebuilds failed. At 0.0.793 every part keeps its working size and no counted builder, transform or coordinate system is left. Build time is not slower. In 36 back-to-back pairs of 15 uncached builds, three rounds for each of the 12 parts with every pair that another process overlapped run again, the best minimum build time at 0.0.793 is 0 to 6% below 0.0.789's on every part. The legacy kernel benchmark ran throttled on a shared host, so its build and edit times are not compared, but its memory after 50 edits fell from 127.1 to 100 MiB for the holed plate and from 238.9 to 199.1 MiB for the gear and plate. The booleans read SimplifyResult's tolerance, Replicad's 0.001 mm, from the new precision role kernelBooleanSimplifyMm; the precision version stays 2, as no role changes value or meaning.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. Geometry is unchanged: every part in the parity set, every benchmark step among them, builds byte-identical preview buffers, volumes, solid counts and bounds, and each adapter returns the same BRep as the Replicad call it replaces.

checklist.schema: No CAD document, sketch, UPID, post, machine package, saved revision, worker message, storage or journal change. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3. CAD_PRECISION_VERSION stays 2: the new role kernelBooleanSimplifyMm carries the 0.001 mm Replicad already passed, so no role changes value or meaning and no cache keyed on it is invalidated.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation, input-version or WebMCP change. A rebuild runs the same native operations in the same order and deletes their builders and temporaries as it goes.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change and no new application controls.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change. Kernel geometry, previews and STEP and STL exports are unchanged.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change.
checklist.verification: New unit suites: cadKernelBuilders (fuse, cut, common, translate, rotate, mirror through XY, XZ and YZ, scale, and all-edge fillet and chamfer each serialize to the same BRep as Replicad's own call, character for character; each deletes its builder, raw result and every point, direction, vector and axis it makes, and leaves its inputs valid; each deletes its builder and keeps its inputs valid when its native builder fails through cadKernelBuilderFactory; the extrusion vector and the revolve axis along three directions equal Replicad's and leave no temporary; CadKernelPlane at three frames gives Replicad's Plane and the same sketch wire, refuses a null normal or x direction and releases what it made, and leaves no vector or axis of the plane or of a sketch placed on it; faces with 0, 1 and 2 holes match Replicad's sketch faces), cadKernelParity (16 parts and 24 bodies, every benchmark step among them, plus a near-full-turn circular pattern, compared with fingerprints of volume, solid, face and edge counts, bounds and an FNV-1a hash of the exact preview buffer bytes, recorded on 0.0.789 with Replicad's own operations; all 24 match, also after the merge with 0.0.792) and cadKernelRebuildMemory (20 back-to-back rebuilds of the benchmark holed plate leave no counted builder, transform or coordinate system after any rebuild and keep the OpenCascade heap the same size; one build each of revolve-mirror-transform, datum-pad-revolve, loft-sweep-pocket, shell-fillet, box-chamfer-all and near-full-turn-pattern leaves none). The precision policy test pins kernelBooleanSimplifyMm at 0.001 in the version 2 record and orders it between kernel confusion and tessellation. The fault-injection tests of cuts, distance cuts, Pocket, loft, sweep, linear and circular patterns, shape ownership, sketches and datum planes, and the Join count spies, moved from Replicad's shape prototypes to cadKernelBuilderFactory and cadKernelBuilders with the same assertions. Mutations, each reverted. Round 1, 11 mutations against the 461 kernel tests: deleting no boolean builder fails 31 tests, no boolean raw result 28, no transform builder 22, no gp_Trsf 22, no fillet builder 2, no chamfer builder 2, no plane 1 and no sketch face builder 2, and skipping the second Build() fails 19, including the near-full-turn parity part; the axis temporaries and the model's revolve axis survived, so the native-object watch was added. Round 2, 15 mutations against the 78 tests of the new and converted suites: the axis temporaries fail 5, the model's revolve axis 2, the second Build() 4, the scaled vector 3, the translation vector 2, the rotation axis 4, the mirror axis 7, direction 6 and origin 6, the scale origin 2, the plane constructor 1, the sketch Ax2 temporaries 3, the sketch axis 10 and the face holes 1; only the extrusion vector's last intermediate survives, as Multiplied returns it and no constructor watch can see it, and main already deletes it the same way. Memory over 100 rebuilds in fresh modules, 0.0.789 at ef007299 against this branch, 12 parts settled and 13 back to back: settled, 5 of the 12 grew by 27.1 to 244.1 MiB on 0.0.789 and none here; back to back, they grew by up to 979.1 MiB and the imported STL body cut by a slot from 1,543.1 to 4,023.1 MiB with 5 of 100 rebuilds failing, against no growth and no failure here; after the final collection 0.0.789 left a gp_Trsf and two gp_Ax3 for every sketch placement and a transform builder for every pattern copy, mirror and transform, and this branch left none of the counted classes. Build time: 36 back-to-back pairs of 15 uncached builds after 2 warm-ups, three rounds for each of 12 parts with the order alternating by round, and 7 pairs run again because another session's process overlapped them; the best minimum here is 0 to 6% below 0.0.789's on every part, and single-round paired ratios range from 0.90 to 1.06. Two pairs of the legacy cad:benchmark ran throttled on this shared machine, with calibration from 60 to 270 ms against 57 to 84 ms for the recorded baseline, and the second overlapped another process in all five attempts, so their build and edit times are not compared; their memory after 50 edits fell from 127.1 to 100 MiB for the holed plate and from 238.9 to 199.1 MiB for the gear and plate, and stayed at 100 MiB for the box fillet (docs/maintainers/cad-performance.md). After merging main at 0.0.792 (1e396001): full Vitest 618 files and 7070 tests pass; npm run build, lint (zero findings, including the precision literal check over 602 files), ui:check and check-release on its own and against origin/main pass. Single Chromium specs, each alone with 2 workers on a production build: cad-kernel (2), cad-workflow (32) and cad-plane-selection-section (6), all passed. No controller or machine verification is claimed.

publicNotes.summary: Long CAD editing sessions no longer use more and more memory.
changes: Rebuilding a part after an edit releases the kernel memory the previous build used. Parts with patterns, cuts or imported bodies no longer grow the kernel's memory with every edit until rebuilds slow down or fail.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged. Parts build the same geometry as before.
